items.title: Higher oil = higher energy? It’s not that simple
items.excerpt: Key points: Energy is becoming more relevant in portfolios again. Middle East disruption has revived the role of energy as a geopolitical and inflation hedge, while Venezuela shows how the global supply map can also evolve. Energy is not one trade. Oil producers, refiners, pipelines, LNG, power generators and grid companies sit at different points of the value chain and respond to very different drivers. The longer-term opportunity is broadening beyond traditional hydrocarbons. EVs challenge road-fuel demand, but AI, electrification, LNG, nuclear and grid investment are creating another energy investment cycle. Why energy matters again Energy is back on investors radar for two very different reasons. The first is geopolitics . Renewed tensions in the Middle East and disruption around the…

items.title: Euro FX futures hold near 1.1650 as CVOL ticks higher.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures traded near unchanged on Thursday, hovering around the 1.1650 level after drifting lower from last week's highs above 1.17. The market continues to take its cues from U.S. Dollar strength, even as expectations remain for a 25 bps rate hike from the European Central Bank next month. Volatility steadily edged higher throughout the week, reflected in the CVOL index, as traders position themselves for the Jackson Hole economic symposium. Friday's session will bring additional data points, including the Chicago Purchasing Managers index and University of Michigan sentiment, though market attention remains squarely on the scheduled 9:00 a.m. address from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

items.title: Euro FX futures slide as inflation data supports dollar.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures experience a near-term pullback following their late August cycle high, navigating a mix of U.S. inflation figures and supportive European economic data. Core PCE in the U.S. held firm at 3.3% year-over-year, keeping higher-for-longer interest rate debates active and providing underlying support for the dollar. Conversely, the euro finds some domestic strength as August PMI figures reflect improving manufacturing conditions, led by Germany. Additionally, German second-quarter GDP saw an upward revision to 0.3%, potentially easing recessionary fears and providing the European Central Bank with flexibility to maintain restrictive policy.

Plus, a look ahead at upcoming Treasury auctions, key tech earnings and jobless claims data.

items.title: From escalation to exit ramp: why oil's war premium is unwinding again
items.excerpt: Key Points: Crude prices have fallen sharply as Iran-Oman talks, Pakistani mediation and other signals raise hopes that Washington and Tehran are searching for a way to de-escalate. The price move is running well ahead of the physical recovery, with Hormuz vessel traffic still severely depressed and Gulf energy infrastructure remaining disrupted. Diesel and gasoil cracks have fallen from extreme peaks but remain exceptionally elevated as Gulf refinery outages and Russian export restrictions continue to constrain supply. The biggest downside risk is a meaningful reopening of Hormuz, while the upside risk is that markets have priced a diplomatic breakthrough that proves much harder to deliver.
